tier_rationale: A purely passive surge suppressor: metal oxide varistors, toroidal chokes, ferrite inductors and capacitors feeding isolated filter banks, plus a mechanical circuit breaker and status LEDs. The manufacturer's own datasheet lists every component and control on the unit and none of them is a radio, microcontroller, app, or network interface.
the_unplug_test: This device does not know your router exists. It is a metal box full of varistors and chokes between the wall and your equipment, with three LEDs that light from the AC line itself, not from any logic. Losing internet changes nothing about it, ever, because nothing in it was ever connected to anything.

repairability.notes: Sealed metal enclosure; Eaton does not publish a component repair guide. The datasheet notes the protection circuit permanently disconnects outlets if it is spent, which is the intended end-of-life signal rather than a fault to repair.

sources.supports: Full manufacturer datasheet: 3330 joules, 6 NEMA 5-15R outlets in 3 isolated filter banks, 120V/12A, MOV+choke+capacitor suppression components, mechanical circuit breaker, diagnostic LEDs, automatic permanent shutoff at end of protection life. No electronics beyond passive suppression components and LED indicators; no app, network, or wireless feature listed anywhere in the spec table.
Manufacturer support/product page confirming current model listing and availability of the owner's manual, with no setup app or account referenced.

notes: Tripp Lite (now sold under the Eaton brand) makes this exact isolated-filter-bank Isobar design in several outlet counts and cord lengths; the ULTRA suffix and metal housing are the identifying marks against cheaper plastic Tripp Lite strips that may use simpler MOV-only protection.
